output_full:
nen.nl — NEN-EN 1757:2022 en — 2022 — https://www.nen.nl/en/nen-en-1757-2022-en-296530
(found by the search; not opened or cited)
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: I take from the NEN-EN 1757:2022 en (E30) that pedestrian-propelled trucks up to and including 500 kg must have a parking brake, and I take from the Ergonomics Case for Folding Hand Trucks: What Safety Research Says About Protecting Workers (E29) that European Standard (EN) 1757 requires stability testing by tilt-table.
Manager said about it: Mara Voss, Kenji Tanaka, Elena Ruiz and Tomas Lind, no blocking objection is settled because the descent-hold objection stands since the rule that trucks to 500 kg need a parking brake from the NEN-EN 1757:2022 en (E30) plus the de-rate from 60 kg flat to 40 kg on stairs from the Trolleys Stair Climbing Trolley 6 Wheels Aluminium Folding Hand Cart Steps | Fruugo SK (E3) proves an auto-lock is needed but no torque is shown, so Elena Ruiz with Kenji Tanaka must prove locked hold with no back-drive and Mara Voss must prove twin-tube stress at full 60 kg on the 197 mm riser, and I answer all four not-ready votes as correct because the device cannot yet carry full load downstairs with one-person hold and fold into the van.
Kenji Tanaka — Stair-Climbing Locomotion said about it: Without the lock the hand must still meet the climb simulation (E23) at about 209 N pull and about 188 N hold, so I confirm what Elena Ruiz takes from the ergonomics push-pull guidance (E28) on sustained limits and from the parking-brake rule for trucks to 500 kg (E30): release must mean locked.

statements.text: I take from the NEN-EN 1757:2022 en (E30) that pedestrian-propelled trucks up to and including 500 kg must have a parking brake, and I take from the Ergonomics Case for Folding Hand Trucks: What Safety Research Says About Protecting Workers (E29) that European Standard (EN) 1757 requires stability testing by tilt-table.

Mara Voss, Kenji Tanaka, Elena Ruiz and Tomas Lind, no blocking objection is settled because the descent-hold objection stands since the rule that trucks to 500 kg need a parking brake from the NEN-EN 1757:2022 en (E30) plus the de-rate from 60 kg flat to 40 kg on stairs from the Trolleys Stair Climbing Trolley 6 Wheels Aluminium Folding Hand Cart Steps | Fruugo SK (E3) proves an auto-lock is needed but no torque is shown, so Elena Ruiz with Kenji Tanaka must prove locked hold with no back-drive and Mara Voss must prove twin-tube stress at full 60 kg on the 197 mm riser, and I answer all four not-ready votes as correct because the device cannot yet carry full load downstairs with one-person hold and fold into the van.

Without the lock the hand must still meet the climb simulation (E23) at about 209 N pull and about 188 N hold, so I confirm what Elena Ruiz takes from the ergonomics push-pull guidance (E28) on sustained limits and from the parking-brake rule for trucks to 500 kg (E30): release must mean locked.
